caveats: The PR describes this as a dummy proof-of-concept crate reserved for future V8 experiments, not a shipped user feature.
The PR body notes likely compatibility drift in the Windows Bazel builder and says Windows Bazel support still needs follow-up work.
proof_points: The PR body explicitly says the new dummy `v8-poc` project demonstrates that Codex can successfully link and use V8 on the platforms it wants to target.

`codex-rs/Cargo.toml` adds a new `v8-poc` workspace member and pins `v8 = =146.4.0`, while `codex-rs/v8-poc/src/lib.rs` adds a proof-of-concept crate with tests that initialize V8 and evaluate an expression.

`MODULE.bazel`, `third_party/v8/BUILD.bazel`, and the Rust CI and release workflows add target-specific V8 artifact wiring, including musl overrides and Bazel-side source-built archives for shipped platforms.
summary: Merged PR #15203 adds a `v8-poc` crate plus Bazel and CI wiring that proves Codex can link and run V8 across the main supported non-Windows target platforms.
title: Codex adds a cross-platform V8 integration proof of concept
watch_state: Watch for follow-up PRs that replace the dummy crate with a real V8-backed feature or re-enable the Windows Bazel path.
why_it_matters: This does not expose a new end-user feature yet, but it gives Codex a verified integration path for embedding V8 in future runtime or tooling work without treating cross-platform linking as an open risk.
